questions.question_english:
Consider the following statements regarding the fundamental objectives of the Contract Labour (Regulation and Abolition) Act, 1970:
I. To abolish contract labour wherever possible and practicable.
II. To ensure that contractors operate without the need for government licensing.

regulate the employment of contract labour
in establishments where complete abolition
is not feasible and to abolish contract labour
in processes where abolition is practicable.
Contractors are strictly required to obtain
official licenses rather than operating without
oversight, ensuring full regulatory compliance
and statutory worker protection.
